## Cost and lifecycle delta

- **Production canary:** the same version command and real-extension child launch sites remain. Three fixed barrier session events (two hook answers, one tool answer), one joined fact, line buffering and bounded fact listeners are in-process/stdIO work. They add no shell, process, polling loop or fixed sleep.
- **Barrier waits:** the existing 10-second per-step deadline bounds fact waits; timeout is reported as a failed contract run. Existing child-stdin close, awaited exit and 3-second kill fallback remain. No retry loop or resident worker was added.
- **Delay fixture:** two one-shot 50-ms timers per split data chunk (one timer for end/close), only in the regression parent. It wraps the already-created stderr stream and launches nothing. It is passed as a direct parent --import, not introduced into normal production invocation.
- **New SDK regression:** on a machine with Copilot, one availability `copilot --version` probe and one Node canary-driver child per suite invocation. That driver performs its normal version query, extension-child launch and existing ancestry probes. Therefore the unit adds **one complete canary run plus one version probe**, not merely one Node process. Without Copilot, discovery attempts the version probe and the integration case skips.
- **New seven-case sensor regression:** ctx.exec is stubbed for every sensor; it exercises the real finite checks logic but launches no commands, tests or builds.
- **Existing ps probes:** ancestry traversal is unchanged and on demand. Round one observed two ps calls, but that is not a universal bound: time spent awaiting pipe delivery can let the real extension progress further through its pre-existing bounded ancestry walk. No claim is made that every delayed test must launch exactly two ps processes.
- **Scheduling:** doctor/self-check/checks remain explicit on-demand entry points. No daemon hook, seat receiver, status line or timer invokes this check. Zero added launches/s at rest; extra unit-process cost scales with test-suite invocations, not live seats.

The #257 recipe/shared-build changes visible in the old-head-to-new-head comparison are rebase content already merged on main, not new #259 process sites. No new daemon spawn site exists; spawn_sites.rs remains unaffected.

Readline processing and three protocol round trips are cheap at the exercised fixed workload. Invalid report-status handling adds only finite array/status processing and no launches. No fleet-wide throughput claim is made, and no controlled before/after fleet experiment was substituted for the direct exact-head command proof above.
